spec.description: An Alexander Calder hanging mobile: a hair-thin black spine carrying five alternating balance arms with black counterweights, hung from a steel hook and ceiling plate, holding nine hand-cut flat leaves in bold primaries that float in mid-air.
spec.layout: A Calder mobile hangs in the air and never touches the floor: the top anchor (cream ceiling plate + steel hook ring) sits at y=2.70 and the lowest leaf bottom is at y=0.18. From the front (+Z): the hook and plate sit centred at x=0; a black spine rod drops 1.46 m down the centre. Five thin black balance arms pierce the spine at pivot collars, alternating direction: arm1 long to the LEFT (y=2.42), arm2 long to the RIGHT (y=2.14), arm3 long to the LEFT (y=1.84) with a second sub-arm branching further left from its tip, arm4 long to the RIGHT (y=1.52), arm5 long to the LEFT (y=1.24, the lowest). Each short side carries a black counterweight (ball or disc) that balances the long side; each long tip carries a hair-thin black string holding a flat, hand-cut Calder leaf in orange, yellow, blue, red or cream, one large black fan among them. All leaf plates face the viewer (+Z) with a slight y-rotation for life, and leaves sit at slightly different depths via the strings. The style is unmistakable Calder: razor-thin black rods and strings, flat organic cut-out shapes in primaries, black hardware, and perfect visual balance between weight and leaf.
